title: Effective Federal Funds Rate (DFF) — 2026-04-24
summary: The Effective Federal Funds Rate (DFF) held steady at 3.64% from April 20–24, 2026, with zero change over the latest observation period. This flat reading reflects stable overnight lending conditions within the current FOMC target range.
key_points: Rate constant across five consecutive trading days (2026-04-20 through 2026-04-24)
why_it_matters: The EFFR is the foundational short-term interest rate for the U.S. financial system, directly influencing money market rates, adjustable-rate loans, and short-term credit conditions. A stable EFFR indicates the Fed's current target range is being effectively maintained by market participants.
macro_context: The EFFR at 3.64% sits within the FOMC's stated target range (3.50%–3.75% floor), implying an unchanged policy stance. No monetary policy decision, statement, or speech accompanies this data point.
market_structure_context: The EFFR is calculated by the NY Fed as a volume-weighted median of overnight federal funds transactions. Stable readings indicate orderly market functioning within the Fed's operating band.
